title: ops-career-experimentation-log-marcus
body:
Purpose: capture small experiments, evidence, and short scripts I can use in 1:1s with my manager. Keep this lightweight — living lab, not final narrative.

Context / signal: I want to shift from execution-heavy contributor to a visible ops strategist who can own cross-functional initiatives and influence roadmap choices. Current role: IC3 (People Ops), primary scope: onboarding, tooling, and ops analytics. Over-indexed on tactical tickets lately.

6-month north star (qual + quant):
- Qual: be the go-to person for two cross-team initiatives (one platform/tooling, one org design) that are explicitly credited in the Q3 roadmap.
- Quant: reduce average onboarding time by 18% for new PM/Eng hires (metric source: onboarding-dashboard), and run 3 post-launch retros with documented action items.

90-day experiments (small, measurable):
1) Rapid toolkit: prototype a lightweight onboarding dashboard (MVP) using existing data sources + 1 pager. Goal: demo to platform lead in 4 weeks.
   - success signal: demo feedback >= 3/5, first stakeholder commit to use in team kickoff.
   - blockers: access to HR raw tables, ETA on data pulls.

2) Influence sprints: schedule 3 30-min syncs with PM leads to map onboarding pain points and propose 2 quick fixes.
   - success signal: at least one PM commits a small change (template/process) to adopt.

3) Visibility routine: publish a 1-paragraph weekly update (2–3 bullets) to #people-ops and tag platform/product.
   - success signal: 2 cross-team comments or follow-ups within week.

Evidence log (micro-evidence entries):
- 2026-02-20: Drafted dashboard layout; got initial thumbs-up from Ava; notes: simplify fields, emphasize time-to-first-PR.
- 2026-02-27: Ran interview w/ PM lead Priya — she confirmed onboarding docs are the main bottleneck not tooling. Action: prioritize doc templates.
- 2026-03-03: Published week 1 update; platform engineer Sam opened follow-up convo (good).

Manager prep script (two-minute pitch + ask):
- One-sentence anchor: "I’ve been running focused experiments to reduce onboarding time and to make our platform more discoverable for new hires; early results show a clear doc gap we can close quickly."
- What I need: one-week of contractor data-access time (or short help from infra) plus endorsement to speak with product onboarding PMs.
- Why it matters: small changes here reduce time-to-productivity and lower support load on platform engineers.
- Ask framing: "Can I have your go-ahead to allocate a short data pull window and a 30-min intro to the onboarding PM next week?"

Meeting agenda for 1:1 (compact):
- 2 min: quick wins (finished demo outline, PM convo)
- 6 min: experiment updates + where I need support (data access, stakeholder intro)
- 6 min: career signal check — what would success look like from your perspective this quarter?
- 6 min: negotiation ask — small guardrails to reclaim focus (pulling back on ticket triage).

Performance signals I want to surface (and evidence to collect):
- Output: adoption of two suggested process changes (evidence: change-requests, PRs).
- Influence: at least 3 stakeholder comments in the shared doc or channel threads.
- Business impact: measurable change in onboarding time (-18% target) or qualitative feedback improvements in new hire survey.

Quick asks (concrete & timeboxed):
- Request data pull for NTD onboarding steps for last 6 months — 2 days of infra time max.
- 30-min intro to product onboarding PM (week of Mar 15).
- Buffer: designate one morning per week (3 hrs) as deep work time for me to focus on experiments.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: tool/data access takes too long -> Mitigation: start with manual sampling + PM interviews to validate hypothesis before full data pull.
- Risk: perceived scope creep -> Mitigation: propose 2-week pilot, with pre-agreed success metrics and automatic sunset if no traction.

Notes to self (raw):
- Keep updates short — one paragraph + 1 metric or ask. Don’t over-explain.
- Use stakeholder language: emphasize "time to value" and "reliability for new hires".
- When describing impact, connect to engineering time saved (convert onboarding time to hours saved).

Open questions (to resolve this week):
- Where is the canonical onboarding data table? Who owns it? (Probably infra analytics team — ask Samir.)
- Is there an existing onboarding survey we can reuse? (Search: CONFLUENCE-1147)

Desired micro-commitments (this sprint):
- T1: Build sample dashboard CSV with two cohorts (PMs vs Eng) — due Thu Mar 12.
- T2: Run 4 PM/stakeholder interviews — complete by Mar 18.
- T3: Draft 1-paragraph update + one ask for manager — send before next 1:1.

Retrospective prompts (for after 90 days):
- Which experiment had the highest signal-to-effort ratio?
- What evidence changed stakeholder behavior?
- What did I learn about navigating priority trade-offs in this org?

Scratchpad quick thoughts (bullet-style):
- If we can get the data, compute median time-to-first-PR and correlate with onboarding doc usage.
- Consider a "starter playbook" template that auto-populates from role/stack.
- Small win: standardize mentor check-in cadence in week 1.

Next actions (today):
- Ping Samir for data-owner intro (Slack DM).
- Sketch CSV sample from internal HR export (local copy).
- Add interview questions to this doc (short list).

Interview question starters (3–5 mins each):
- "When did you feel equipped to ship? What was missing?"
- "Which onboarding artifact did you use most in week 1?"
- "If you could remove one friction, what would it be?"

Closing note to self: Keep iterations small, track evidence in the log above, and treat manager as a partner for clearing constraints rather than as an approver for small bets.
